questions.title: Number Series - Increasing Differences
questions.questionText: Find the next number in the series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 4, 6, 8, 10, so the next difference is 12 and the next term is 30 + 12 = 42.

questions.title: Number Series - Geometric Progression
questions.questionText: Find the next number in the series: 3, 9, 27, 81, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is multiplied by 3: 81 x 3 = 243.

questions.title: Number Series - Squares Plus One
questions.questionText: Find the next number in the series: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?

questions.title: Number Series - Double and Add One
questions.questionText: Find the next number in the series: 5, 11, 23, 47, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the previous term plus 1: 47 x 2 + 1 = 95.

questions.title: Number Series - Fibonacci Pattern
questions.questionText: Find the missing number: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ?, 21
questions.explanation: Each term is the sum of the two before it. 5 + 8 = 13, and 8 + 13 = 21 confirms it.

questions.title: Number Series - Growing Differences
questions.questionText: Find the next number in the series: 7, 10, 14, 19, 25, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 3, 4, 5, 6, so the next difference is 7: 25 + 7 = 32.

questions.title: Number Series - Decreasing Differences
questions.questionText: Find the next number in the series: 100, 95, 85, 70, 50, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are -5, -10, -15, -20, so the next is -25: 50 - 25 = 25.

questions.title: Syllogism - Chain of All Statements
questions.questionText:
Statements: All cats are dogs. All dogs are birds.
Conclusions: I. All cats are birds. II. Some birds are dogs.
questions.explanation: I follows by chaining 'All cats are dogs' and 'All dogs are birds'. II follows because 'All dogs are birds' implies that some birds are dogs.

questions.title: Syllogism - Some and All
questions.questionText:
Statements: Some pens are books. All books are tables.
Conclusions: I. Some pens are tables. II. All tables are books.
questions.explanation: The pens that are books are also tables, so I follows. II reverses 'All books are tables', which is not allowed.

questions.title: Syllogism - Negative Statement
questions.questionText:
Statements: No flower is a tree. Some trees are plants.
Conclusions: I. Some plants are not flowers. II. No plant is a flower.
questions.explanation: The plants that are trees cannot be flowers (no flower is a tree), so some plants are not flowers. II is too strong: other plants may be flowers.

questions.title: Blood Relations - Father's Brother's Son
questions.questionText: Pointing to a photograph, Riya says, 'He is the son of my father's only brother.' How is the man related to Riya?
questions.explanation: My father's brother is my uncle, and his son is my cousin.

questions.title: Blood Relations - Generation Chain
questions.questionText: A is B's sister. C is B's mother. D is C's father. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation: C is the mother of both A and B, and D is C's father. So A is D's daughter's daughter, i.e. his granddaughter.

questions.title: Blood Relations - Only Daughter of My Mother
questions.questionText: Introducing a man, a woman says, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the woman related to the man?
questions.explanation: The only daughter of the woman's mother is the woman herself, so she is the man's mother.

questions.title: Direction Sense - Return Path
questions.questionText: A man walks 5 km north, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 5 km. How far, and in which direction, is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: North 5 km, then east 3 km, then south 5 km brings him back to the same latitude, 3 km east of the start.

questions.title: Direction Sense - Turning Angles
questions.questionText: Rohan faces East. He turns 90 degrees clockwise and then 180 degrees anticlockwise. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: East turned 90 degrees clockwise is South. Turning 180 degrees from South gives North.

questions.title: Direction Sense - Four Legged Walk
questions.questionText: Aman starts at P and walks 10 m west. He turns left and walks 10 m, then turns right and walks 10 m, then turns right again and walks 10 m. Where is he with respect to P?
questions.explanation: West 10 m, left (south) 10 m, right (west) 10 m, right (north) 10 m. Net: 20 m west and 0 m north-south.

questions.title: Coding-Decoding - Letter Shift
questions.questionText: In a certain code, ROAD is written as URDG. How is SWIM written in that code?
questions.explanation: Every letter is moved 3 places forward (R->U, O->R, A->D, D->G). So S->V, W->Z, I->L, M->P gives VZLP.

questions.title: Coding-Decoding - Next Letter
questions.questionText: If MONDAY is coded as NPOEBZ, how is FRIDAY coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by the next letter of the alphabet: F->G, R->S, I->J, D->E, A->B, Y->Z.

questions.title: Coding-Decoding - Reverse Order
questions.questionText: If TABLE is coded as ELBAT, how is CHAIR coded?
questions.explanation: The word is written backwards: TABLE -> ELBAT, so CHAIR -> RIAHC.

questions.title: Ranking - Position from the Other End
questions.questionText: In a row of 40 students, Ravi is 12th from the left. What is his position from the right?
questions.explanation: Position from the right = total - position from the left + 1 = 40 - 12 + 1 = 29.

questions.title: Seating - Five Friends in a Row
questions.questionText: Five friends A, B, C, D and E sit in a row facing north. A is to the left of B but to the right of C. D is to the right of B but to the left of E. Who sits in the middle?
questions.explanation: C is left of A, A is left of B, B is left of D, D is left of E. The order is C, A, B, D, E, so B is in the middle.

questions.title: Ranking - Total Students from Two Ranks
questions.questionText: In a class, Priya ranks 7th from the top and 28th from the bottom. How many students are in the class?
questions.explanation: Total = rank from top + rank from bottom - 1 = 7 + 28 - 1 = 34.

questions.title: Analogy - Place of Work
questions.questionText: Doctor : Hospital :: Teacher : ?
questions.explanation: A doctor works in a hospital in the same way a teacher works in a school.

questions.title: Odd One Out - Planets
questions.questionText: Which one is different from the others: Mercury, Venus, Moon, Mars?
questions.explanation: Mercury, Venus and Mars are planets. The Moon is a natural satellite of the Earth.

questions.title: Synonym - Abundant
questions.questionText: Choose the word closest in meaning to ABUNDANT.
questions.explanation: Abundant means existing in large quantities, which is the same as plentiful.

questions.title: Antonym - Benevolent
questions.questionText: Choose the word opposite in meaning to BENEVOLENT.
questions.explanation: Benevolent means well-meaning and kind. Malevolent means wishing harm to others.

questions.title: One Word - Lover of Books
questions.questionText: Choose the single word for 'a person who loves books'.
questions.explanation: A bibliophile loves books. A philatelist collects stamps, a numismatist collects coins, and a misanthrope dislikes people.

questions.title: Sentence Correction - Subject-Verb Agreement
questions.questionText: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
questions.expectedAnswer: Neither of the students has submitted the assignment.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular, so it takes the singular verb 'has', and 'of the students' needs the plural noun.

options.text: Neither of the students have submitted the assignment.
Neither of the student has submitted the assignment.
Neither of the students has submitted the assignment.
Neither of the students are submitting the assignment.

questions.title: Fill in the Blank - Preposition
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: She is allergic ____ peanuts.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'allergic' is followed by the preposition 'to'.

questions.title: Idiom - Bite the Bullet
questions.questionText: What does the idiom 'to bite the bullet' mean?
questions.expectedAnswer: To face a painful or unpleasant situation bravely
questions.explanation: It means to accept an unpleasant but unavoidable situation and deal with it with courage.

options.text: To face a painful or unpleasant situation bravely

questions.title: Reading Comprehension - Photosynthesis
questions.questionText:
Passage: 'Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants prepare food using sunlight, carbon dioxide and water. Oxygen is released as a by-product.'
Which gas is released during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: The passage states that oxygen is released as a by-product.

questions.title: Encapsulation - Hiding Internal State
questions.questionText: Which OOP principle bundles data with the methods that operate on it and restricts direct access to the internal state?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation keeps fields private and exposes controlled access through methods.

questions.title: Compile-Time Polymorphism
questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of compile-time (static) polymorphism?
questions.explanation: Overloaded methods are chosen by the compiler from the argument types. Overriding is resolved at run time.

questions.title: Abstract Class vs Interface
questions.questionText: Which statement about an abstract class and an interface in Java is TRUE?
questions.expectedAnswer: An abstract class can have constructors and instance fields, an interface cannot have instance fields
questions.explanation: Abstract classes can hold state and constructors. Interfaces only declare constants (static final fields), and a class can extend only one class.

options.text: An abstract class can have constructors and instance fields, an interface cannot have instance fields
An interface can have constructors, an abstract class cannot
Both can be instantiated directly with new
A class can extend multiple abstract classes

questions.title: Concrete Class and Abstract Methods
questions.questionText: A non-abstract class extends an abstract class but does not implement one of its abstract methods. What happens?
questions.explanation: A concrete class must implement every inherited abstract method or be declared abstract itself.

options.text: The method returns null at run time
The program compiles and the method does nothing
An exception is thrown only when the method is called

questions.title: Constructors and Inheritance
questions.questionText: In Java, are constructors inherited by subclasses?
questions.expectedAnswer: No, a subclass must declare its own constructors
questions.explanation: Constructors are not members that are inherited. A subclass constructor calls a superclass constructor with super(...).

options.text: No, a subclass must declare its own constructors

questions.title: Implicit super() Call
questions.questionText: A superclass declares only a constructor that takes an int parameter. A subclass constructor does not call super(...) explicitly. What happens?
questions.expectedAnswer: Compilation error, because there is no no-argument superclass constructor to call implicitly
questions.explanation: The compiler inserts an implicit super() call. If the superclass has no accessible no-argument constructor, the subclass must call a constructor explicitly.

options.text: It compiles and the int parameter defaults to 0
Compilation error, because there is no no-argument superclass constructor to call implicitly
It compiles and fails with an exception at run time

questions.title: Multiple Inheritance and the Diamond Problem
questions.questionText: How does Java avoid the diamond problem that arises with multiple inheritance?
questions.expectedAnswer: A class can extend only one class, but may implement many interfaces
questions.explanation: Single class inheritance removes ambiguity. For interfaces with conflicting default methods, the class must override the method.

options.text: A class can extend only one class, but may implement many interfaces
It merges the methods of all parents automatically
It picks the parent that was declared first

questions.title: Virtual Functions in C++
questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of virtual functions in C++?
questions.expectedAnswer: To enable run-time polymorphism through the base class pointer or reference
questions.explanation: A virtual call is dispatched on the actual object type (via the vtable), not the pointer type.

options.text: To prevent a class from being inherited
To allow functions without a body
To enable run-time polymorphism through the base class pointer or reference

questions.title: Static Methods and Instance Members
questions.questionText: Which statement about a static method in Java is correct?
questions.expectedAnswer: It cannot directly access non-static instance fields
questions.explanation: A static method belongs to the class, so it has no this reference and cannot use instance members without an object.

options.text: It must be called on an object
It cannot directly access non-static instance fields
It can be overridden to change run-time behaviour

questions.title: Composition - Has-A Relationship
questions.questionText: A Car class contains an Engine object. Which relationship does this describe?
questions.explanation: Using another object as a field is composition. Inheritance describes is-a relationships.

questions.title: SOLID - Single Responsibility Principle
questions.questionText: What does the Single Responsibility Principle state?
questions.expectedAnswer: A class should have only one reason to change
questions.explanation: Each class should focus on one responsibility so changes to one concern do not ripple into others.

options.text: A class should have only one reason to change
A class should have only one method
A class should extend only one class
A class should be instantiated only once

questions.title: SOLID - Liskov Substitution Principle
questions.questionText: What does the Liskov Substitution Principle require?
questions.expectedAnswer: Objects of a subclass must be usable wherever the superclass is expected without breaking correctness
questions.explanation: Subtypes must honour the contract of the base type. A Square that breaks the behaviour of Rectangle's setters is a classic violation.

options.text: A subclass must have more methods than its parent
Every class must implement an interface
Subclasses must not call parent methods
Objects of a subclass must be usable wherever the superclass is expected without breaking correctness

questions.title: SOLID - Open/Closed Principle
questions.questionText: What does the Open/Closed Principle say?
questions.expectedAnswer: Software entities should be open for extension but closed for modification
questions.explanation: You should be able to add new behaviour (for example, a new subclass) without editing existing, tested code.

options.text: Classes should be open to the public and closed to subclasses
Methods should never be changed once written
Software entities should be open for extension but closed for modification

questions.title: SOLID - Dependency Inversion Principle
questions.questionText: What does the Dependency Inversion Principle recommend?
questions.expectedAnswer: High-level modules should depend on abstractions, not on concrete implementations
questions.explanation: Depending on interfaces lets you swap implementations (for example, a database) without changing the business logic.

options.text: Low-level modules should depend on high-level modules directly
High-level modules should depend on abstractions, not on concrete implementations
Dependencies should be created using new inside the class
Every class should have a single dependency

questions.title: SOLID - Interface Segregation Principle
questions.questionText: What does the Interface Segregation Principle state?
questions.expectedAnswer: Clients should not be forced to depend on methods they do not use
questions.explanation: Prefer several small, focused interfaces over one large one.

options.text: Clients should not be forced to depend on methods they do not use
An interface should contain as many methods as possible
A class should implement only one interface

questions.title: Singleton Pattern
questions.questionText: What does the Singleton design pattern guarantee?
questions.expectedAnswer: Only one instance of the class exists and it has a global access point
questions.explanation: Singleton restricts instantiation to one object and provides access to it.

options.text: Every call creates a new object
Objects are created only from subclasses
Only one instance of the class exists and it has a global access point

questions.title: Factory Pattern
questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of the Factory pattern?
questions.expectedAnswer: To create objects without exposing the instantiation logic to the client
questions.explanation: A factory method returns objects of a common type, so client code does not depend on concrete classes.

options.text: To ensure only one object is created
To notify observers of state changes
To create objects without exposing the instantiation logic to the client
To add behaviour to an object at run time

questions.title: Observer Pattern
questions.questionText: Which design pattern defines a one-to-many dependency so that when one object changes state all its dependents are notified?
questions.explanation: A subject keeps a list of observers and notifies them of changes, as in event listeners.

questions.title: Strategy Pattern
questions.questionText: Which pattern encapsulates a family of interchangeable algorithms so the algorithm can be chosen at run time?
questions.explanation: Strategy moves each algorithm into its own class behind a common interface (for example, different sorting or payment strategies).

questions.title: Decorator Pattern
questions.questionText: What does the Decorator pattern let you do?
questions.expectedAnswer: Add responsibilities to an object dynamically without subclassing
questions.explanation: Decorators wrap an object that has the same interface and add behaviour before or after delegating to it.

options.text: Hide a complex subsystem behind a simple interface
Add responsibilities to an object dynamically without subclassing

questions.title: final Keyword on a Class
questions.questionText: What does declaring a class final mean in Java?
questions.explanation: A final class (for example String) cannot have subclasses.

questions.title: Dynamic Method Dispatch Output
questions.explanation: The reference type is A but the object is a B. The overridden method is chosen at run time, so B.show() runs.

questions.title: Overload Resolution
questions.questionText: A class has two methods: void f(int x) and void f(long x). Which is called by f(5)?
questions.explanation: The literal 5 is an int, so the exact match f(int) is preferred over a widening conversion to long.

options.text: The call is ambiguous and does not compile

questions.title: Immutable Class Example
questions.questionText: Which of the following Java classes is immutable?
questions.explanation: Once created, a String's contents cannot change. Methods like concat return a new String.

questions.title: equals() and hashCode() Contract
questions.questionText: If two objects are equal according to equals(), what must be true about their hashCode() values?
questions.explanation: The contract requires equal objects to have equal hash codes. Otherwise hash-based collections like HashMap break.

questions.title: Upcasting
questions.questionText: Assigning a subclass object to a superclass reference variable is called:
questions.explanation: Upcasting is implicit and always safe. Downcasting needs an explicit cast and can fail at run time.

questions.title: protected Access
questions.questionText: Which Java access modifier allows access within the same package and also from subclasses in other packages?
questions.explanation: protected members are visible in the package and to subclasses. Package-private is visible only inside the package.

questions.title: Instantiating an Abstract Class
questions.questionText: Can you create an object of an abstract class directly using new?
questions.expectedAnswer: No, only of a concrete subclass
questions.explanation: Abstract classes are incomplete by design. You instantiate a concrete subclass instead.

options.text: Yes, if it has no fields
Yes, if the constructor is public
No, only of a concrete subclass

questions.title: Virtual Destructors in C++
questions.questionText: Why should a base class that is used polymorphically have a virtual destructor in C++?
questions.expectedAnswer: So deleting a derived object through a base pointer calls the derived destructor
questions.explanation: Without a virtual destructor, deleting through a base pointer is undefined behaviour and the derived part may not be destroyed properly (leaks).

options.text: So the class cannot be copied
So deleting a derived object through a base pointer calls the derived destructor
So the object is deleted automatically

questions.title: Cohesion and Coupling
questions.questionText: Which combination do good object-oriented designs aim for?
questions.explanation: Classes should be focused (high cohesion) and depend on each other as little as possible (low coupling).

questions.title: Static Method Hiding
questions.questionText: A subclass declares a static method with the same signature as a static method in its superclass. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Static methods are bound to the class, so the subclass method hides the parent's one. The choice depends on the reference type, not the object.

questions.title: Marker Interface
questions.questionText: Which of these is a marker interface in Java (an interface with no methods)?
questions.explanation: Serializable has no methods. It only marks that a class's objects can be serialized.

questions.title: ARP - Mapping IP to MAC
questions.questionText: Which protocol is used to find the MAC address that belongs to a known IP address on a local network?
questions.explanation: The Address Resolution Protocol broadcasts a request and the owner of the IP replies with its MAC address.

questions.title: DHCP - Automatic Configuration
questions.questionText: What does DHCP do?
questions.expectedAnswer: Automatically assigns IP addresses and network settings to devices
questions.explanation: A DHCP server leases an IP address, subnet mask, gateway and DNS server to each client.

options.text: Translates domain names into IP addresses
Automatically assigns IP addresses and network settings to devices
Converts private addresses to public ones

questions.title: Subnet Mask for a /26 Network
questions.questionText: Which subnet mask corresponds to the prefix length /26?

questions.title: NAT - Private to Public Translation
questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of Network Address Translation (NAT)?
questions.expectedAnswer: To let devices with private IP addresses share a public IP address
questions.explanation: NAT rewrites source addresses and ports so many internal hosts can reach the internet through one public address.

options.text: To encrypt packets between two hosts
To let devices with private IP addresses share a public IP address

questions.title: HTTP 429 Status Code
questions.questionText: Which HTTP status code tells a client it has sent too many requests (rate limiting)?
questions.explanation: 429 is returned when a client exceeds a rate limit and often includes a Retry-After header.

questions.title: Switch vs Hub
questions.questionText: Which device forwards frames using MAC addresses at the data link layer?
questions.explanation: A switch learns which MAC address is on which port and forwards frames only to the right port. A hub repeats traffic to every port.

questions.title: TLS - What It Provides
questions.questionText: Which set of guarantees does TLS provide for a connection?
questions.expectedAnswer: Encryption, authentication of the server and message integrity
questions.explanation: TLS encrypts traffic, authenticates the server with a certificate, and detects tampering.

options.text: Encryption, authentication of the server and message integrity

questions.title: Distance-Vector Routing Protocol
questions.questionText: Which of the following is a distance-vector routing protocol?
questions.explanation: RIP shares its routing table with neighbours and uses hop count. OSPF and IS-IS are link-state protocols.

questions.title: ICMP - Ping
questions.questionText: Which protocol does the ping command use to test reachability?
questions.explanation: Ping sends ICMP Echo Request messages and waits for Echo Replies.

questions.title: Idempotent HTTP Methods
questions.questionText: Which HTTP method is idempotent, meaning repeating the same request has the same effect as sending it once?
questions.explanation: PUT replaces a resource with the given representation, so repeating it leaves the same result. POST usually creates a new resource each time, and PATCH is not guaranteed to be idempotent.

questions.title: IMAP vs POP3
questions.questionText: How does IMAP differ from POP3?
questions.expectedAnswer: IMAP keeps messages on the server and syncs them across devices
questions.explanation: POP3 typically downloads and removes mail from the server, while IMAP leaves it there. SMTP is used to send mail.

options.text: IMAP keeps messages on the server and syncs them across devices
IMAP is used to send email and POP3 to receive it
IMAP can only be used on one device

questions.title: WebSocket vs HTTP
questions.questionText: What is the main advantage of a WebSocket connection over repeated HTTP requests for a chat application?
questions.expectedAnswer: A persistent full-duplex connection so the server can push messages
questions.explanation: After the upgrade handshake, client and server can send messages at any time over one connection.

options.text: It makes pages load without JavaScript
A persistent full-duplex connection so the server can push messages

questions.title: Content Delivery Network
questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of a Content Delivery Network (CDN)?
questions.expectedAnswer: To serve content from servers geographically close to users
questions.explanation: Caching static assets at edge locations reduces latency and load on the origin server.

options.text: To assign IP addresses to clients
To serve content from servers geographically close to users

questions.title: Role of a Router
questions.questionText: Which device connects different networks and forwards packets between them using IP addresses?
questions.explanation: Routers work at the network layer and choose the next hop for each packet using their routing tables.
